 Farioli on Académico: “The competition never changes our preparation” 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Francesco Farioli, FC Porto ’s head coach, looks ahead to the home match against Académico de Viseu with a warning about the opposition’s form and an assurance of rigorous preparation. With injuries ruling out players and the sections reserved for organised supporters’ groups closed, the coach wants his team ready to respond to a match with its own particular challenges. And he makes the guiding principle of his work clear: “The competition’s logo never affects our preparation.”
 FC Porto are preparing to host a team that has returned to the top flight and is enjoying a run of form that deserves attention. In his preview, Francesco Farioli put commitment above the fixture list and the name of the competition, without downplaying the obstacles: from Académico’s performances to the players available, his message was one of focus and readiness.
 OneFootball Videos
 The coach’s first warning concerned the opposition. Farioli highlighted the Viseu side’s run of results and linked that recognition to the need for Porto’s players to rise to the demands of the match.
 “Académico de Viseu are on a fantastic run of results,” said the coach, who wants his players to “rise to the challenge and be ready for anything”. He anticipated a “different kind of game”, which had been “prepared for with the same commitment as always”.
 Respect for Académico is therefore more than a routine pre-match formality. In the coach’s view, FC Porto’s response must begin with their preparation and extend to their ability to adapt during the game.
 That commitment, Farioli explained, does not depend on where a match falls in the calendar. The coach advocated consistently high standards, linking them to the need to keep the entire squad ready to compete.
 “At big clubs, the schedule is always packed,” he stressed, insisting that “the competition’s logo never affects our preparation”.
 To illustrate that point, the coach compared very different stages of a season. The approach, he maintained, remains unchanged.
 “The preparation for the first pre-season game or for the Europa League quarter-finals was the same, always with the same commitment and high standards,” he explained. Farioli insisted that “every game is equally important” and that it is necessary to have “every player ready to play, because the season is long and everyone in the squad will have a role to play”.
 Rather than setting priorities between competitions, the coach emphasised continuity in their work. In that reasoning, squad management is a necessity over a long season, making each player’s preparation all the more important.
 In the stands, things will look different because of the closure of the sections reserved for organised supporters’ groups. Farioli did not hide his sadness at their absence, but expressed confidence that the remaining fans could provide the team with the support they need.
 The situation “makes him sad”, the coach acknowledged. “The stadium will be full, so the support we usually hear coming from those sections will have to be recreated by the roughly 45,000 people in the stands.”
 The appeal places responsibility for maintaining a supportive atmosphere on the rest of the stadium. Without ignoring the impact of the closure, Farioli sought to rally those who will be in the stands.
 As for selection options, the wings received particular attention. Mateus Mide took part in the final training session and will be included in the matchday squad, while Vasco Sousa, William Gomes and Oskar Pietuszewski are confirmed absentees through injury.
 Mateus Mide’s involvement in training was due to the “lack of options on the wings”, Farioli explained. Regarding William Gomes, the coach said the Brazilian winger “is still dealing with pain, but he is already feeling better and starting to work on the pitch”, while cautioning that “it is difficult to give an exact date for his return”.
 William Gomes is making progress, but there is still no firm timetable for his return. For now, the absences limit the available choices and reinforce the importance of having alternatives ready.
 Their opponents will be an Académico side that finished second in the Segunda Liga and returned to the top flight after 37 years. The team is now coached by Bruno Pinheiro, with whom Farioli worked in Qatar, and has retained two key figures from last season: André Clóvis, the leading scorer with 23 goals, and Soufiane Messeguem, the leading assist provider with 10.
 Alongside the continuity provided by those key players, the squad has undergone an overhaul. Seven players departed, while goalkeepers Ewerton, from Barra-SC, Marcos Lavín, from USL Dunkerque, and Juan Soriano, from Leganés, arrived.
 In midfield, Académico signed Andro Babic from Velez Mostar, Alejandro Mestanza from Atlético de Madrid and Cristian Ferreira from Argentinos Juniors. In attack, João Guilherme arrived from EC Água Santa, Mohamed Bouldini from RC Deportivo, Valery Fernández from Real Zaragoza, Álvaro Zamora from Aris and Paulinho from Wieczysta Krakow.
 The eleven most-used players include goalkeeper Ewerton and defenders Robinho, Anthony Correia, Nikos Michelis and Gustavo Costa. That core is completed by midfielders Soufiane Messeguem, Cihan Kahraman and Luís Silva, along with forwards João Guilherme, Lorougnon Gohi and André Clóvis.
 André Clóvis leads the team’s scoring charts with four goals, followed by João Guilherme with three and Soufiane Messeguem with two. Cihan Kahraman leads the way with four assists in a side that combines key figures from the promotion campaign with new arrivals.
 The Portuguese Football Federation’s Refereeing Committee has appointed Sérgio Guelho, from the Guarda Football Association, to officiate the match. The 35-year-old referee will be assisted by André Pontes and José Mira, with Flávio Jesus serving as fourth official. Manuel Oliveira will oversee VAR, assisted by Tiago Leandro.
